title: Khadijah
hook: She was a successful businesswoman. She hired him, watched him, and then she proposed.

screens.text: **She was one of the most respected traders in Makkah.** She hired a young man to take her goods to Syria, watched how he worked, and then she proposed.

**A businesswoman hires him.** Khadijah bint Khuwaylid was a wealthy, respected widow with a trading business. She hired him to take her goods to Syria, and he came back with a good profit [IslamQA 34550; Qalam ep. 20].
bubbles: Remember his nickname: al-Amin, "the trustworthy". Someone you could trust with your goods on a long trip was worth a lot.

screens.prompt: He came back from Syria with her goods sold well. What do you think impressed Khadijah most?

options.feedback: Right. The sources say his honesty is what impressed her, and it's what led her to propose.
Not quite. He had very little money. She was the wealthy one. It was his character that won her over.
Not quite. He was a poor orphan raised by his uncle. She was impressed by his honesty.

screens.text: **She proposed.** Impressed by his honesty, Khadijah sent a friend, Nafisah, to ask whether he would marry her. He agreed [IslamQA 34550; Qalam ep. 21].
bubbles: He was about 25. She was older: most reports say forty, though some give a younger age [IslamQA 11575; Qalam ep. 21].

screens.text: A marriage of about 25 years, and loyalty that outlived it.

events.title: A trading trip
events.text: Khadijah hires him to take her goods to Syria. He returns with a good profit [IslamQA 34550; Qalam ep. 20].

events.title: A proposal
events.text: Impressed by his honesty, she proposes through her friend Nafisah [IslamQA 34550; Qalam ep. 21].

events.title: One marriage
events.text: He marries no one else as long as she lives [Muslim 2436; Yaqeen].

events.title: Never forgotten
events.text: He speaks of her often and sends gifts of meat to her friends [Bukhari 3818].

events.title: A quarrel at the Ka'bah
events.text: At about 35, he settles a dispute that could have turned into a fight [IslamQA 11575].

screens.text: **Greetings from her Lord.** Once, as Khadijah was on her way to him with food, **Jibril** came. He told the Prophet ﷺ to greet her with peace from her Lord, and to give her good news of a house in **Jannah** (Paradise) [Bukhari 3820].
bubbles: The hadith describes that house as a place with no noise and no tiredness [Bukhari 3820].

cards.back: He married no one else, for about 25 years [Muslim 2436].
He still spoke of her often. When he slaughtered a sheep, he sent portions to her friends [Bukhari 3818].
She was never as jealous of anyone as of Khadijah, a woman she never even met, because he talked about her so much [Bukhari 3818].

screens.text: **Built on character.** She didn't choose him for money; he had little. She chose him for how he handled her goods when nobody was checking. And he honoured her for the rest of his life.
bubbles: Her business and her proposal weren't frowned on. Muslims tell her story with pride.

screens.situation: Keisha runs a small cleaning business. A coworker at her part-time job hears she became Muslim and asks, "So now you'll have to give up your business and stay home?"

options.text: Tell her about Khadijah: a businesswoman the Prophet ﷺ worked for, married, and honoured all his life
options.feedback: Yes. Khadijah ran her own trade and was deeply honoured. Questions about Keisha's own situation can go to her imam.

options.text: Agree that it's probably expected of her now
options.feedback: Not quite. The Prophet's ﷺ first wife ran a business. Don't assume the worst; ask the imam about specifics.

options.text: Get defensive and end the conversation
options.feedback: Not quite. It's a fair question with a great answer. A calm story does more than an argument.

screens.text: She chose him for his character, and he honoured her long after she was gone. Character and loyalty are what last.

check.prompt: How did Khadijah come to marry him?

options.text: She hired him, saw his honesty, and proposed through a friend
options.feedback: Right. She watched how he worked, then sent her friend Nafisah to propose.

options.text: His uncle arranged it for money
options.feedback: Not quite. Khadijah herself proposed, through a friend, after seeing his honesty.

check.prompt: How did he treat Khadijah's memory after she died?

options.text: He spoke of her often and sent gifts to her friends
options.feedback: Right. Even Aisha said she was jealous of no one as much as of Khadijah [Bukhari 3818].
Not quite. He spoke of her so often that Aisha said she was jealous of her [Bukhari 3818].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, a respected, wealthy Makkan widow, hired him to take her goods to Syria; he made a good profit [IslamQA 11575; IslamQA 34550; Qalam ep. 20]. IslamQA 34550 adds that her servant Maysarah went with him (not on screen).
- Impressed by his honesty, she proposed through her friend Nafisah [IslamQA 34550; Qalam ep. 21].
- He was about 25. Her age is disputed: most reports say forty; some scholars report 28 to mid-30s [IslamQA 11575; Qalam ep. 21; Yaqeen]. Say "older than him; most reports say forty".
- He married no one else while she lived [Muslim 2436], about 25 years [Qalam ep. 55; Yaqeen].
- Years after her death he spoke of her often and sent meat to her friends; Aisha said she was jealous of no one as much as of Khadijah [Bukhari 3818].
- Jibril brought Khadijah greetings of peace from her Lord and good news of a house in Paradise with no noise or toil [Bukhari 3820].

**Likely questions**
- *"How old was Khadijah?"* Older than him; most reports say forty, some give a younger age. Don't pick one as certain.
- *"Why did he marry more wives later?"* He was married to Khadijah alone for about 25 years; his later marriages were mostly to widows or divorcees, many tied to alliances and care. Keep it to that, and offer "Ask my imam" for more. (scholar question Q41)
- *"How old was Aisha?"* Not this episode's topic. If pressed, follow the track's approach: the sahih reports give six at the contract and nine when the marriage began [Bukhari 5133]; scholars discuss it; never mock the question or deny the hadith; offer the imam. (scholar question Q37)
- *"Can a woman propose? Can Muslim women work?"* Khadijah proposed through a friend, and she ran her own trade; Muslims honour both. How a marriage is arranged today (the wali, the contract) and any personal work question go to the imam; Day 42 and Day 66 cover marriage.
- *"Did they have children?"* Yes; seerah-40 covers his children. Bukhari 3818 mentions that he had children from her.

**Escalate:** any personal marriage question (choosing a spouse, a current marriage to a non-Muslim, Q21 territory); teens asking about marriage go to the imam and their family.

**Don't**
- Don't give Khadijah's age as certain.
- Don't use this episode to pressure anyone toward marriage, or to rank women by whether they work.
- Don't compare his wives with each other.
- Don't picture the Prophet ﷺ, Khadijah or Jibril.
